correctness.rationale: Direct graph incidence definition produces 24 arcs and exactly 12,800 augmented faces (independent enumerations agree). The deterministic matching has 5,887 augmented pairs and 297 critical four-simplices plus 729 critical five-simplices, with full acyclicity established by topologically sorting all 60,480 directed Hasse incidences. Removing the empty pair leaves one critical vertex. The signed integer gradient-path formula gives a 297x729 boundary matrix with 4,162 initial nonzero entries; integer unit elimination performs exactly 297 unimodular pivots, so the four-skeleton attaching-degree matrix has invariant factors all 1 and zero remainder. Since π4 of a wedge of four-spheres is free on their inclusions, this CW model is homotopy equivalent to 432 five-spheres. Independent full mod-two simplicial reduction gives ranks (1,23,211,981,2376,2592), validating dimension counts; the matrix–forest Euler value 432 provides a separate check. The code proves only this fixed finite instance.

value.rationale: Scoville–Zaremsky explicitly identify homotopy types of complete-bipartite graph Morse complexes as meaningful unknown objects; K3,4 is the smallest unbalanced example with a part of size three just beyond the published K3,3 and K2,n cases. The result resolves its exact homotopy type, not merely its Euler characteristic or Betti vector. The signed 297-pivot analysis excludes nontrivial integral attaching behavior, yielding a concrete test case for rooted-forest spaces and computational discrete Morse topology.
